findings.statement: Higher baseline OSM is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), but the UNIFI placebo arm does not separate after correction (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]) and the drug-vs-placebo interaction is not significant, so this is weak evidence of a drug-specific mechanism. Golimumab shows nothing after correction (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]).

TREM1 is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), which points to a severity marker rather than a ustekinumab-specific mechanism. Nothing survives correction for golimumab, infliximab or vedolizumab.

CXCL8 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]) but equally with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]); the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.981]), so it marks severity, not a drug mechanism.

In the adalimumab single-cell atlas (GSE282122; a small cohort of remitters and non-remitters), CXCL8 shows no baseline cell-state difference between non-remission and remission; it changes after treatment in a few epithelial and mononuclear phagocyte states (higher in undifferentiated enterocytes and transit-amplifying cells, lower in cycling MNPs), which is a lead from a small cohort only.

CXCR2, the leading gene of the convergence ranking, is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.00000969]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), again consistent with a neutrophil-related severity signal.

IDO1 does not separate ustekinumab non-responders after correction (padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.14]) yet does separate UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0289]), so it is a severity-type signal with no drug-specific association.

TNF transcript is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=TNF; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.00969]) but not in golimumab non-responders (padj [gene=TNF; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]); no anti-TNF arm shows an association after correction.

TNFa pathway activity is higher in non-responders to ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]), but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]) while not in PURSUIT placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]); the signal is largely general severity.

JAK-STAT pathway activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but not in vedolizumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]).

CHRDL2 is a first-in-class candidate whose transcripts are mainly stromal (inflammatory fibroblasts); the stromal lineage is replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122. Gaps: only part of the increase is retained after composition adjustment, and its highest vital-organ RNA is [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM.

LAX1 is up in [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=8] cohorts and is a first-in-class candidate, but its lineage does not replicate: Smillie 2019 assigns it to T/NK while Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 assign plasma cells (only GSE282122 agrees), and only part of the increase is retained after composition adjustment, so it may reflect immune infiltration.

XKR9 is classed as intrinsic (epithelial lineage, replicated in Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122; Garrido-Trigo 2023 disagrees), but it is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts and is expressed by a small percentage of epithelial cells, so replication of the increase is thin.

GLT1D1 is classed as composition-driven: its inflamed-mucosa neutrophil share is [gene=GLT1D1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.891] and the myeloid lineage replicates in all three other atlases, so the signal reflects infiltrating neutrophils rather than a change of the tissue itself.

caveats: Response cohorts are small except UNIFI; golimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab, etrolizumab and ACT1 arms have no gene surviving correction in the genes checked.
Association only; no gene here is shown to predict response.
The adalimumab single-cell atlas (a small cohort of remitters and non-remitters) was queried only for OSM (no significant cell-state difference) and CXCL8.
Only a minority of the first-in-class discovery candidates were profiled in detail; CPXM1, HAPLN3, FIBIN and others were not.
Top convergence-ranking genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8, CD274, IDO1, MMP1) are neutrophil/inflammation-driven and largely severity markers.
